title: CDU-SPD Coalition Agrees Reform Roadmap With July 15 Deadline After Six-Hour Crisis Meeting
detail: After weeks of deadlock and public recriminations, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU/CSU-SPD coalition held a marathon six-hour meeting and agreed on a comprehensive reform agenda to be pushed through parliament before the summer recess on July 15. The package includes income tax relief targeted at small and medium enterprises and partnerships, a pension system overhaul, healthcare restructuring, and a 'bureaucracy cabinet' session on July 15 to cut red tape by AI-reviewing over 20,000 business proposals. Merz called pension reform 'the toughest nut to crack in the coming months.' The agreement came as polls showed the coalition was widely seen as dysfunctional, with 75% of voters saying it was failing and 58% predicting it would not survive to 2029.

media.caption: Germany's CDU-SPD coalition agrees July reform roadmap after crisis summit; pension and tax reform central

title: SPD Beats AfD 66-34% in Brandenburg District Runoff — Coalition's Rare Local Win
detail: In a runoff election for District Administrator of Barnim in Brandenburg, SPD candidate Daniel Kurth won decisively with 66.1% of the vote, defeating the AfD challenger who received 33.9%. The result provided a rare bright spot for the governing coalition, demonstrating that AfD's national polling strength does not automatically translate into local electoral wins — particularly in runoffs where centrist and left voters consolidate against the far right. Brandenburg state overall still shows AfD performing strongly, with the party leading state polls at around 30%, but the Barnim result showed the limits of AfD's one-on-one runoff appeal.

media.caption: SPD's Daniel Kurth wins Brandenburg Barnim district runoff 66-34% over AfD challenger
